summary: Messenger, mail, and social REST runtime JSON write routes can now opt into existing tenant-scoped SQL write-plan and transactional-outbox command plans through a local recording executor.
claim_boundary: This slice binds messenger, mail, and social implemented REST JSON write routes to existing service-owned REST write-plan entrypoints and records tenant-scoped SQL/outbox command execution through RecordingSqlBatchExecutor. It proves local loopback command-plan composition, required tenant SQL header enforcement, ordered command names, and response/audit metadata only. It does not connect to a live Postgres/Citus database, run SQLx transactions, drain or publish a broker outbox, prove Kubernetes Gateway/TLS/ArgoCD/OpenCost behavior, claim a live Oyatie Cloud substrate, claim remote CI green, or deploy a production tenant workload. FD-001 product delivery remains the master-plan product goal; Oyatie Cloud is the future dogfood substrate/proof point.

Grounds the ordered tenant-scope command contract and RecordingSqlBatchExecutor used for loopback evidence without live database I/O.

repo_local_context.use: Before this slice, messenger/mail/social runtime routes bound only stateless JSON handlers, while SQL write-plan recording mode existed only for community.
Messenger app plans already compose usecase receipts, tenant-scoped SQL write batches, protocol events, transport plans, and transactional outbox append.
Mail app plans already compose submission receipts, tenant-scoped SQL write batches, protocol events, transport plans, and transactional outbox append.
Social app plans already compose post receipts, tenant-scoped SQL write batches, protocol events, transport plans, and transactional outbox append.

findings: Adds one explicit opt-in BackboneSqlWriteState rather than changing default messenger/mail/social JSON route behavior.
Extracts shared REST request builders so JSON-write and SQL-write paths reuse the same edge parsing logic instead of duplicating field mapping.
Messenger, mail, and social now expose the same local REST-to-SQL/outbox recording seam as community, closing a parity gap for future FD-001 tenant workload integration.
The claim remains local/recording only; no live Oyatie Cloud substrate, live database, broker, Gateway, ArgoCD, OpenCost, remote CI, or production workload evidence is asserted.
RED focused cargo test failed before implementation because BackboneSqlWriteState, with_stateless_sql_write_state, and stateless SQL route-count support did not exist.

GREEN focused tests prove messenger/mail/social SQL write-plan responses record insert_messenger_message, insert_mail_message, insert_social_post, and insert_transactional_outbox_event command batches and reject missing SQL tenant headers before execution.
Callers opt into BackboneSqlWriteState explicitly and can inspect execution_reports for deterministic local evidence.
Route counts report sql_write_plan=1/json_write=0 for opt-in stateless SQL mode, making the bound behavior auditable.
Focused cargo tests, crate lib tests, fmt, check, and clippy all pass for the touched runtime crate.
Default route-catalog counts remain covered, and new tests cover both success and required SQL tenant headers.
Rejected adding live SQLx execution to the shared REST runtime adapter; live database I/O remains isolated in SQLx adapter/runtime seams.
Rejected changing default routes to SQL write-plan mode because existing loopback callers depend on stateless JSON behavior and honest opt-in boundaries.
No secrets, credentials, connection strings, or tenant production data fixtures are added.
SQL write-plan mode requires explicit tenant scope, home cell, shard key, and jurisdiction headers before constructing TenantSqlContext.
All SQL statements are generated by existing parameterized command-plan builders and are not assembled from HTTP body strings in this adapter.
Default runtime path is unchanged. The opt-in SQL write-plan path uses local mutex-protected recording state for tests only and performs no network/database I/O.
The added dispatch work is bounded to one implemented write route per stateless service and does not add background loops or unbounded collection growth beyond caller-inspectable test reports.
Responses preserve policy_decision_ref, idempotency_key, audit_correlation_id, application_name, tenant-scoped command names, and explicit non-claim text for audit review.
Rollback removes the optional stateless SQL write-plan state mode, shared request-builder refactor, tests, and task/evidence updates without a data migration or public REST contract removal.
Execution reports expose application_name, ordered command names, command count, and transaction_committed from the recording executor; no live telemetry emission is claimed.

Default build_backbone_rest_router output remains unchanged for messenger/mail/social callers: implemented write routes still use runtime_handler=json_write unless stateless SQL state is explicitly supplied.
Community local in-memory and community SQL write-plan modes remain available and covered by existing tests.
Uses existing CS-BACKBONE slice naming and explicit sql_write_plan runtime-handler terminology.
Updates task plan/todo and multispectrum evidence only; no new root Markdown or retired coordination surface.
Runtime binding remains in the shared backbone REST runtime adapter; service-owned write-plan logic remains in messenger/mail/social REST/app crates.
The adapter reuses service-owned REST/app write-plan seams and the shared command kernel recording executor; it does not import sqlx or peer persistence adapters.
No new Cargo dependencies are added in this slice; it reuses the command-kernel dependency already present in the runtime adapter.
No database migration, OpenAPI schema, proto, or algorithm changes. Existing SQL write batches/outbox statements are reused.
Focused local checks pass; full oya verify --ci-required will be recorded before submit. Remote CI green is not claimed.
